provenance: Agent-authored before first retrieval run; no human validation. Expected labels and source_check are scoring-only and must never enter tag construction, retrieval or generation prompts.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. I want to learn why the median can describe skewed incomes better than the mean. Give a small worked example.
questions.source_check: Explain sensitivity to extreme values without claiming the median is always superior.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. I want to learn standard deviation and variance, including their units and what happens if every measurement is doubled.
questions.source_check: Distinguish standard deviation scaling by 2 from variance scaling by 4.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. Teach me how random sampling differs from random assignment, and which permits a causal conclusion.
questions.source_check: Separate generalization to a population from causal inference under experimental assumptions.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. I want to read histograms. Use a figure from a book to explain skew, shape, and an outlier.
questions.source_check: A linked histogram must support described shape and values; do not invent plotted data.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. I want to learn conditional probability with a two-way table and a worked calculation.
questions.source_check: Correctly choose the conditioning denominator.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. Help me distinguish mutually exclusive events from independent events, with a counterexample.
questions.source_check: Explain why disjoint events with positive probabilities cannot be independent.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. I want to learn when a binomial model is appropriate and solve a short example.
questions.source_check: Check fixed trials, independence, two outcomes and a common probability.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. Explain the central limit theorem and why it does not make the raw data normally distributed.
questions.source_check: Identify the sampling distribution and applicable assumptions.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. Teach me how to interpret a 95 percent confidence interval, including a common incorrect interpretation.
questions.source_check: Use repeated-sampling coverage, not a post-data probability about a fixed parameter.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. I want to understand a p-value. Does p = 0.03 mean the null hypothesis has a 3 percent chance of being true?
questions.source_check: Condition on the null and assumptions; reject posterior interpretation.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. Teach me type I error, type II error and power using one consistent example.
questions.source_check: Keep the same null, alternative and decision definitions throughout.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. I want to choose between a paired t-test and an independent samples t-test for before-and-after observations.
questions.source_check: Use differences within pairs, with appropriate assumptions.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. I want to learn why running many t-tests is risky and what an ANOVA tells me.
questions.source_check: Explain multiplicity and omnibus versus pairwise conclusions.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. Use a scatterplot from the textbooks to explain correlation without implying causation.
questions.source_check: Inspect the selected plot; distinguish association, confounding and causal design.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. I want a worked example interpreting a regression slope and intercept, and why extrapolation is dangerous.
questions.source_check: Use consistent units, observed range and one primary source example.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. Teach me the molecular steps of CRISPR gene editing from these books.
questions.source_check: State missing biology coverage and do not invent textbook support.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. I keep mixing up standard error and standard deviation. Build three exercises that reveal the difference.
questions.source_check: Separate spread of observations from variability of an estimator.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. I want to learn how to read a box plot using an actual textbook figure, including the whiskers and outliers.
questions.source_check: Follow the displayed source convention for whiskers; do not assume they always mean min and max.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. Explain why a screening test with high sensitivity can still produce many false positives when prevalence is low.
questions.source_check: Apply Bayes rule or a frequency table, keeping sensitivity distinct from positive predictive value.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. Teach me how a residual plot can reveal that a straight-line model is inappropriate. Use a textbook plot.
questions.source_check: Inspect the plot for systematic pattern rather than assert good fit from a large correlation.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. I want to learn why a small p-value does not establish a large or useful effect.
questions.source_check: Distinguish statistical from practical significance with sample-size context.

questions.query: I'm taking an introductory undergraduate statistics course. Teach me how prior information and new data combine in Bayesian inference, then give a short exercise.
questions.source_check: Keep Bayesian posterior language separate from frequentist confidence coverage.

questions.query: I'm a high-school beginner. Help me distinguish nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio measurements with examples and a self-check.
questions.source_check: Explain ordered categories, equal intervals and meaningful zero.

questions.query: I'm studying advanced mathematics. I want a rigorous proof of the spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators from these textbooks.
questions.source_check: State absent scope; incidental eigenvalue or factor-analysis mentions are insufficient.
